comment: Ids reserved for records in preparation - assigned but not yet published. Reserved ids are permanent: they will publish when verified, and are never reused for anything else. Neutral by design; no record content lives here. Distinct from retired ids (rejected candidates, CVE convention), listed under `retired`: an id that was assigned to a candidate in a public pull request and then rejected before registration. Retired ids never publish and are never reused; the entry names the date, the rejection reason and the public discussion.

retired.reason: Candidate rejected before registration. The draft recorded a claim, made by LiteLLM during incident response, that a coding agent had written developers' GitHub CLI OAuth tokens into gateway logs behind the litellm 1.107.0 release compromise of 2026-10-21. LiteLLM's canonical 2026-10-23 attack-chain post withdrew that explanation (the first token came from an internal agent-platform API reached with a master key committed to a public repository); no agent action remains, so the event is out of scope.
